record.original_question: For the same join-the-shortest-queue model with stationary ergodic input, what are the minimal assumptions that guarantee uniqueness of the stationary regime?

evidence.quote: Consider again the multi-server (say, 2-server) queue with stationary and ergodic input {t_n, sigma_n}, but assume now that the discipline is join-the-shortest-queue.
So, here are the open problems: what are the minimal requirements for the uniqueness of the stationary regime?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a queueing system with two identical servers fed by a single stationary and ergodic marked point process of arrivals $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$, where $t_n$ denotes the arrival time of the $n$-th customer (with $t_n<t_{n+1}$, $t_n\to\pm\infty$) and $\sigma_n\geq 0$ denotes its service requirement. Upon arrival, each customer is routed under the join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) discipline: customer $n$ enters the server whose current workload (residual work) is the smaller of the two, with ties broken by a fixed deterministic rule. Each server is work-conserving and serves its assigned customers in FCFS order at unit rate. Let $W_n=(W_n^{(1)},W_n^{(2)})$ denote the workload vector seen by the $n$-th arriving customer.

A stationary regime is a distribution on $\mathbb{R}_+^2$ that is invariant under the Palm-stationary dynamics induced by the input $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}$ and the JSQ routing rule, i.e. a probability measure $\pi$ such that if $W_0\sim\pi$ on the Palm probability space of the input, then the resulting bi-infinite workload process is jointly stationary and ergodic with the input.

Determine minimal assumptions on the stationary ergodic input $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}$ (e.g., on the joint law of inter-arrival times and service times, beyond the natural stability condition $\mathbb{E}[\sigma_0]<2\,\mathbb{E}[t_1-t_0]$) under which the stationary regime of the two-server JSQ system is unique.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search did not turn up a result establishing minimal assumptions for uniqueness of the stationary regime of the two-server join-the-shortest-queue system under general stationary ergodic input. Existing work treats either i.i.d./Markovian inputs, heavy-traffic/Halfin–Whitt diffusion limits, or stability and tail asymptotics, but the minimal-assumption uniqueness question for the stationary ergodic JSQ model appears not to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Stationary analysis of the shortest queue problem
status_evidence.snippet: Analytical results for the stationary loss system of two parallel JSQ queues, under specific Markovian/finite-capacity assumptions rather than general stationary ergodic input.
status_evidence.claim: Available stationary analyses of JSQ rely on Markovian or finite-capacity assumptions, not general stationary ergodic ones.

status_evidence.title: Steady-state analysis of the Join the Shortest Queue model in the Halfin-Whitt regime
status_evidence.snippet: Examines steady-state properties of JSQ in a heavy-traffic asymptotic regime, proving exponential ergodicity of the diffusion limit.
status_evidence.claim: Recent steady-state analyses focus on asymptotic regimes rather than minimal assumptions for uniqueness under general stationary ergodic input.

status_evidence.title: A Large Deviation Principle for Join the Shortest Queue
status_evidence.snippet: Large deviations work for JSQ requires establishing uniqueness for infinite-dimensional ODE systems, indicating uniqueness questions for JSQ remain technically delicate.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness questions for JSQ dynamics remain a delicate area of ongoing research.
